\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Left sign family]
\lean{FABL.signPairFamilyLeft}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p134-b009}
\label{FABL.signPairFamilyLeft}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign}
Given a family $\omega$ assigning a pair of signs to each of the $n$ coordinates, the
left sign family is the sign vector whose value at each coordinate is the first sign in
that pair.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Right sign family]
\lean{FABL.signPairFamilyRight}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p134-b009}
\label{FABL.signPairFamilyRight}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign}
Given a family $\omega$ assigning a pair of signs to each of the $n$ coordinates, the
right sign family is the sign vector whose value at each coordinate is the second sign
in that pair.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[A sign monomial correlation]
\lean{FABL.independentSignPair_monomial_right_expectation}
\label{FABL.independentSignPair_monomial_right_expectation}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.independentProductPMF, FABL.monomial, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_one, FABL.pmfExpectation_independentProductPMF_prod, FABL.signPairFamilyLeft, FABL.signPairFamilyRight, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{6}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and at each coordinate $j\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ choose a
probability mass function $p_j$ on pairs of signs and a real number $\rho_j$. Suppose
that under $p_j$ each sign has mean zero, while the product of the two signs has mean
$\rho_j$. For a set $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ and a coordinate $i$, take a tuple of
pairs with the independent product distribution, form the product of its left signs over
$S$, and multiply by its right sign at $i$. The expectation is $\rho_i$ if $S=\{i\}$ and
is zero otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coordinate correlation and Fourier coefficient]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_apply_left_mul_right_eq_fourierCoeff_mul_correlation}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_apply_left_mul_right_eq_fourierCoeff_mul_correlation}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.Sign, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourier_expansion, FABL.independentProductPMF, FABL.independentSignPair_monomial_right_expectation, FABL.monomial, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_mul, FABL.pmfExpectation_sum, FABL.signPairFamilyLeft, FABL.signPairFamilyRight, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and for each $k\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ let $p_k$ be a
probability mass function on pairs of signs and let $\rho_k\in\mathbb R$. Suppose that
under $p_k$ each sign has expectation zero and the product of the two signs has
expectation $\rho_k$. For any function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ and any coordinate $i$,
the expectation of the product of $f$ evaluated on the first sign vector and the $i$th
sign of the second vector, when coordinates are sampled independently according to the
$p_k$, equals $\widehat f(\{i\})\rho_i$, where $\widehat f(\{i\})$ is the uniform
Fourier coefficient of $f$ at the singleton coordinate $\{i\}$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $n$, the majority function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube has
equal first-level Fourier coefficients: for all coordinates $i,j\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$,
its Fourier coefficient at $\{i\}$ equals its Fourier coefficient at $\{j\}$.

\difficulty{4}
Let $n>0$, and let $f:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\{-1,1\\}$ have equal Fourier coefficients at all
singleton sets. For every coordinate $i$, the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $\\{i\\}$ is
at most the Fourier coefficient at $\\{i\\}$ of the majority function, which takes the
sign of the sum of the coordinates and returns $1$ when that sum is zero.
\end{theorem}
